A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, figures, equations, prompt tables, and appendices A-C. Reorganized and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on GPQA and MMLU-Pro-S, including scaling curves, ablations, and analyses connecting empirical outcomes to the theoretical assumptions.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds MATH-500 evaluations and GPQA-diamond experiments with QwQ-32B and GPT-4o.

M1.justification: The knockout tournament and league-style average-win-rate procedures are retained, including generation, pairwise comparisons, and selection rules. Additional model backends and task-specific prompt formatting do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v3 extends evaluation beyond GPQA and MMLU-Pro-S multiple-choice questions to 500 MATH-500 problems requiring mathematical answers. This substantively broadens task requirements; the original datasets and their category coverage remain.

E2.justification: Majority voting remains the principal external comparison method, but its participation changes: v3 adds comparisons on the filtered GPQA subset and with the new GPQA-diamond backends, while omitting the MMLU-Pro-S comparison from v2 Figure 12. Best-of-N remains unevaluated.

E3.justification: v3 adds QwQ-32B and GPT-4o configurations using K=2 and N up to 16 on GPQA-diamond, plus MATH-500 evaluation up to N=32. The original model configurations, MMLU-Pro-S sampling, temperatures, and accuracy metric retain their stated settings.

E4.justification: The filtered-GPQA analysis gains majority-voting comparisons and revised knockout curves. v3 Figure 8 adds generation/comparison-success diagnostics for QwQ-32B and GPT-4o. Existing K and CoT ablations, opponent-subsampling analysis, and knockout-versus-league diagnostics are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions describe independent trials for filtered-subset evaluations. Neither adds explicit run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; pluralized wording does not establish additional repetitions.

E6.justification: v3 adds MATH-500 and QwQ-32B/GPT-4o scaling results. It also changes the filtered-GPQA Mixed result at N=64 from approximately 81% in v2 Figure 4 to 90% in v3 Figure 3, without a stated protocol revision. Filtered-subset majority-voting results are added, while MMLU-Pro-S majority-voting results are removed.

T1.justification: Definition 1, both assumptions, Theorems 1-3, their appendix proofs, and the four assumption-comparison examples retain their mathematical substance. Renaming the league parameter from p_gen to p_cs and compressing equivalent formulas are not theoretical changes.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain two black-box tournament algorithms with conditional exponential or power-law scaling guarantees and empirical support. Broader experiments support these retained claims without changing their theoretical scope or novelty positioning.

C2.justification: v3 expands the interpretation of majority-voting comparisons using LLM-call budgets, explains the exclusion of Best-of-N, and discusses complementarity with long-CoT models. Its revised limitations section drops the explicit discussion of nonbinary metrics and allocation across a fixed collection of problems.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents that MATH-500 prompts receive output-format adjustments, but Tables 1-2 omit v2's explicit system/user-role labels. Temperature, positional balancing, AgentScope, and prompt/parsing-code provenance disclosures are retained, largely relocated to Appendix C.1.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including DeepSeek-R1, Kimi k1.5, s1, and the newly evaluated resources, while removing Damani et al.'s compute-allocation reference. The positioning of theoretical understanding, rather than tournament design itself, as the main novelty remains.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites and condenses the abstract, introduction, experimental narrative, and discussion; adds a contents list and introductory subheadings; and reorganizes Appendix C. Implementation details and much MMLU-Pro-S discussion move out of the main narrative.

P2.justification: Figures are extensively resized, regrouped, and relocated. v3 Figure 5 combines four league analyses, several main-text panels move to the appendix, and new model/dataset panels appear. Many knockout plots switch to logarithmic N axes, and both prompt tables are placed together.

improvement.justification: The added mathematical-task and model evaluations broaden empirical support, and the reorganization improves navigation. However, v3 omits the MMLU-Pro-S comparison showing majority-voting advantages and changes the filtered-GPQA curves while retaining a 25-point-gain explanation inconsistent with the revised Mixed curve. These competing effects on coverage, comparative evidence, and internal consistency prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
